instruction: We act for Fosais Solar Installations, LLC, which is the licensee under a software license arrangement with Dreitoul Software, Inc. Before the client relies on this package, I need a clear view of where it is exposed and what we should push back on. Please review the full matter folder: software_license_agreement.md, side_letter_2026-11-04.md, parent_guaranty.md, and insurance_certificate_cover_letter.md. Treat them together as the deal set; don't limit yourself to the main agreement. Prepare a memo to me listing each issue you identify. For each one, give the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters for Fosais specifically, and recommend a fix. That could be revised language, a request to the counterparty, or a point to confirm with the client. Please rank the issues so the most significant come first, and flag anything you think needs attention before signing or performance. Keep the memo practical and concise. I'd rather see a well-reasoned short list than an exhaustive clause-by-clause summary. If something is ambiguous or you need facts from the client to assess it, note that rather than assuming.

rubric.text: The response identifies that License Agreement Section 4.3 (read with the Section 1.1 definitions of 'Territory' and 'Solar Project') bars Fosais from using any competing product for all project types, including commercial and utility-scale, across the United States and Canada. It also identifies that this is broader than the residential rooftop, Arizona-and-Nevada-only exclusivity scope recorded in Side Letter Recital B. The response locates the issue in the License Agreement exclusivity provision (Section 4.3 and/or the Section 1.1 definitions), explains why this matters to Fosais and recommends a fix.
hints: residential rooftop projects in Arizona and Nevada

rubric.text: The response identifies that License Agreement Section 12.3 excludes Section 11 indemnification obligations from the Section 12.1 liability cap. As a result, Fosais's broad Section 11.2 indemnity for third-party claims arising from its installations is uncapped. The response locates the issue in the License Agreement limitation of liability and indemnity provisions (Section 12.3 and/or Section 11.2), explains why this matters to Fosais and recommends a fix.
hints: arising out of or relating to any Installation

rubric.text: The response concludes that the non-renewal deadline under License Agreement Section 14.1 was October 31, 2026, so the Non-Renewal Notice delivered on November 2, 2026 was late. It also concludes that the License Agreement is therefore at risk of automatically renewing for a further three-year term. The response locates the issue in Side Letter Section 4 and/or License Agreement Section 14.1, explains why this matters to Fosais and recommends a fix.
The response states that the License Agreement prevails over the Side Letter in the event of conflict.
The response states that Fosais Holdings Corp. is the guarantor of Fosais's obligations under the Parent Guaranty.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner in which, for each issue, the document and section are identified.
The response presents the issues in an explicit ranking or order of significance, with the most significant issues first.
The response claims that Fosais's November 2, 2026 Non-Renewal Notice was timely under License Agreement Section 14.1.
The response claims that the Side Letter effectively amends or narrows the License Agreement's exclusivity covenant to residential projects in Arizona and Nevada.
